purpose: THE SINGLE INDIRECTION POINT for review items R1, R6 and R8.
Neither encounter-source.v1.shex nor encounter-target.v1.shex contains a domain class IRI, a person IRI or a practitioner IRI.

encounterClass.note: NOT derived from the FHIR Encounter.class code (v3-ActCode AMB). That code has no reviewed entry in the code-interpretation table, and concept note section 2 forbids treating a code literal as a class assertion. It is bound by the source schema and retained in the source layer.

practitionerRoleClass.source: concept note section 6 example graph writes ex:ClinicianRole; the reviewer overrode it with ex:PractitionerRole on 2026-10-03 (DR-010, answering R8a)
practitionerRoleClass.note: The FHIR participation type PPRF (primary performer) is bound by the source schema and guarded to PPRF, but it does not itself type this role. A reviewed participation-type-to-role-class table is the natural home for that mapping and does not exist yet.
practitionerRoleClass.reviewer_override: The ruling is OntoClean: 'practitioner' names an anti-rigid property, so it must be carried by a Role individual rather than by the person. PractitionerRole is preferred over the note's ClinicianRole because Encounter.participant.individual references a Practitioner, so it is derived from what the record states; ClinicianRole names a clinical function the source did not assert. Leaves R12 free to refine it from a reviewed participation-type table.

personSuloClass.reviewer_words: a person is a Spatial Object.
personSuloClass.note: sulo:SpatialObject rdfs:subClassOf sulo:Object, so hasParticipant's range is still satisfied and the PRO chain is unaffected. The point of the change is the guard it restores: sulo:Feature owl:disjointWith sulo:SpatialObject, so a person also typed as a Quality or a Role is now INCONSISTENT and a reasoner catches it. Bare sulo:Object could not, because Quality subClassOf Feature subClassOf Object. Checked against the pinned ontology before applying: sulo:hasFeature is NOT a subproperty of sulo:hasPart, so `person hasFeature quality` does not trip SpatialObject's `hasPart only SpatialObject` restriction.
personSuloClass.not_recorded_in_policy_yet: As of this change, policies/code-interpretation.v1.json reviewer_decisions holds only R1 and R10. Transcribed from the integration lead's relay of the reviewer's words; see DR-206.

practitionerClass.source: concept note section 6 writes ex:clinician-c7 without saying what it is
practitionerClass.note: R8a is ANSWERED (DR-010): a practitioner IS a person. This stays a separate manifest entry from personClass so the two remain independently rebindable, but both resolve to ex:Person and the identity service now mints both with entity_kind 'person'. Patient/c7 and Practitioner/c7 still do not merge, because resource_type is a key input -- that is record provenance under R2b, not a claim that they are different people.

practitionerSuloClass.reviewer_words: a person is a Spatial Object.
practitionerSuloClass.note: sulo:SpatialObject rdfs:subClassOf sulo:Object, so hasParticipant's range is still satisfied and the PRO chain is unaffected. The point of the change is the guard it restores: sulo:Feature owl:disjointWith sulo:SpatialObject, so a person also typed as a Quality or a Role is now INCONSISTENT and a reasoner catches it. Bare sulo:Object could not, because Quality subClassOf Feature subClassOf Object. Checked against the pinned ontology before applying: sulo:hasFeature is NOT a subproperty of sulo:hasPart, so `person hasFeature quality` does not trip SpatialObject's `hasPart only SpatialObject` restriction.
practitionerSuloClass.not_recorded_in_policy_yet: As of this change, policies/code-interpretation.v1.json reviewer_decisions holds only R1 and R10. Transcribed from the integration lead's relay of the reviewer's words; see DR-206.

recordClass.source: concept note section 6: 'The FHIR Encounter record and its status remain in the source/record layer'
recordClass.note: The concept note names ex:ObservationRecord for section 4 but no class for the Encounter record. ex:EncounterRecord is this map's placeholder and is flagged as a new reviewer question.

person.note: Concept note section 6's ex:person-p123 is an identity output, not a FHIR reference.

practitioner.source: IdentityService.resolve(...) for Encounter.participant.individual, entity_kind person (DR-010: 'practitioner' is anti-rigid and cannot be an entity kind)
practitioner.note: Concept note section 6's ex:practitioner-c7 is an identity output. enc-contained-practitioner resolves a contained '#pr-inline' reference, so the entity IRI differs from enc-baseline's Practitioner/c7 and must not be assumed equal.

node_key_note: These match the concept note section 6 example graph's local names exactly (ex:encounter-9, ex:patient-role-enc-9, ex:practitioner-role-enc-9, ex:interval-enc-9, ex:start-enc-9, ex:end-enc-9).

A ROLE IS KEYED BY THE ENCOUNTER, not by the person. Two encounters give two distinct patient-role nodes, which is correct: a role is a feature of its holder in the context of one process, and merging them would assert one role participating in two processes.
CD-1: host-chosen root nodes declared in MapContract.node_key_rules, not engine-minted.
pass_vars_note: Every target constraint in this map is required, so lastReport.unboundVariables must be empty on every pass, and lastReport.unusedStatics must be empty too. tests/contracts/maps/test_encounter_gate3.py asserts both.
r11_note: R11 changed record->result to sulo:hasPart for the Observation maps. NOT applied here.

`encounter-record sulo:hasPart encounter-process` is inconsistent against SULO 0.2.12: sulo:InformationObject subClassOf (hasPart only InformationObject) would force the process to be an InformationObject and so an Object, but sulo:Object owl:disjointWith sulo:Process; and sulo:Object subClassOf (not (hasPart some Process)) forbids it directly.
A result is information that sits inside a record. An encounter is an event in the world; it is not located in its record. The record sulo:refersTo it.
Reported to the integration lead as a reading, per the R1d asymmetry the reviewer raised.
